steps.thought: List all available tests on the station to see the available options and their costs.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly check all communication buses and device enumerations across the entire unit.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed successfully with all CAN nodes, UART devices, camera sensor, I2C devices, and boot checks returning valid results. This rules out basic hardware connectivity faults and total power-on failures.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power-on self test passed cleanly, suggesting the unit may be healthy, though further subsystem tests are required to confirm.
IMU was detected on I2C during boot, but calibration and sensor accuracy must be tested under static conditions.
ESC nodes were enumerated on CAN, but commutation performance requires telemetry and spin tests.
Compass was detected on I2C, but magnetic interference can only be checked during motor operation.
Unit booted fine, but battery performance under load needs verification.

steps.thought: Run battery_rest_check to verify cell voltages and rest health before moving to active load tests or motor spins.
steps.observation: The battery_rest_check passed cleanly with a pack voltage of 16.594V, cell voltages all around 4.15V, and a very low cell imbalance of 0.012V, ruling out weak cells or battery imbalance at rest.

hypotheses.rationale: Both power-on selftest and battery rest check passed with no failures, indicating a healthy unit so far.
ESCs passed initial CAN enumeration; detailed behavior must be checked via esc_telemetry.
IMU initialized properly on I2C; static sensor performance must be evaluated via imu_static.
Compass initialized properly on I2C; static and dynamic compass tests are required to check for interference.
Battery rest voltages are normal, but internal resistance and load sag need checking via battery_load_test.

steps.thought: I will run esc_telemetry to check commutation and sync stability across all four ESCs, as it is a cheap and direct way to rule out motor/ESC issues.
steps.observation: The esc_telemetry test revealed a high number of sync errors (27) on esc_3, while other ESCs reported normal sync error counts. This points specifically to an ESC commutation or synchronization fault on channel 3.

hypotheses.rationale: ESC 3 reported 27 sync errors in telemetry, significantly exceeding the failure threshold of 5, indicating commutation problems.
High sync errors on ESC 3 could occasionally stem from a motor winding short or phase issue on motor 3.
Remaining possibility that the sync error is an intermittent telemetry anomaly, though unlikely given the high count.

steps.thought: I will run motor_spin_test to check whether esc_3 also shows current or RPM anomalies or if the motor itself has issues on position 3.
steps.observation: The motor_spin_test confirmed severe failure on motor_3 with an abnormal low RPM of 3660 and excessive RPM jitter of 1180, complementing the esc_telemetry failure of 27 sync errors on esc_3. This points strongly to an ESC commutation desync or a motor phase/winding issue on position 3.

hypotheses.rationale: ESC 3 experienced 27 sync errors combined with erratic motor performance on channel 3, strongly suggesting commutation desynchronization.
Severe RPM drop and high jitter on motor 3 could alternatively be caused by a winding short or phase driver issue on motor 3.

steps.thought: Search the failure library to differentiate between ESC_DESYNC and MOTOR_WINDING_SHORT using historical records for motor 3 sync errors and jitter.

args.query: esc_3 sync errors rpm jitter motor_3

matches.title: Motor stutters and loses sync
matches.symptom_summary: One motor stutters during spin up, rpm is low and unstable with very large rpm jitter. ESC telemetry on that channel shows many sync errors while back-EMF is detected. Packet loss is normal on all ESCs.
matches.root_cause: ESC commutation timing set wrong in firmware, causing desync on that channel.
matches.rework_notes: Reflash the ESC on the affected channel with the released firmware and timing profile.

matches.title: ESC overheats and derates under sustained load
matches.symptom_summary: One ESC temperature climbs above 80 C during long runs and the motor rpm drops as the ESC derates. Sync errors low, packet loss normal.
matches.root_cause: Missing thermal pad between ESC FETs and the heatsink.
matches.rework_notes: Install the thermal pad. ESC temperature is the tell.

matches.title: Motor will not spin, ESC sees no back-EMF
matches.symptom_summary: Spin test shows one motor at zero rpm drawing almost no current and staying at room temperature. ESC telemetry for that channel reports back-EMF not detected and zero sync errors. Other three motors normal.
matches.root_cause: Open stator winding (broken magnet wire at the solder cup).
matches.rework_notes: Replace the motor at the dead position. Check the phase wire solder joints on the replacement.

steps.observation: The historical failure records and current telemetry point directly to ESC_DESYNC on channel 3, matching the high sync errors and severe RPM jitter while back-EMF is successfully detected.

hypotheses.rationale: ESC 3 reported 27 sync errors alongside severe RPM drops and huge jitter, matching known ESC commutation desync profiles.
Low RPM and high jitter could potentially stem from a partial winding short, though back-EMF is still detected.

steps.thought: The historical failure records and tests clearly point to an ESC commutation desync on esc_3. I am ready to propose the rework action to reflash the ESC firmware on esc_3.
